# Radical Learn

Radical Learn is a Quizlet-style trainer for radical reactivity in organic chemistry: which radicals are nucleophilic or electrophilic, which partners they react with fastest, and where they add or take a hydrogen atom. Everything is in one HTML file.

**Play it here:** https://chemtrain.github.io/radical-learn/radical_learn.html

You can also download `radical_learn.html` and open it in any browser. Its sister pages are [Reactivity Learn](https://github.com/ChemTrain/reactivity-learn) (nucleophiles, electrophiles and Mayr's scales) and [Photoredox Learn](https://github.com/ChemTrain/photoredox-learn).

## What's inside

- Philicity: is a radical nucleophilic or electrophilic? 29 carbon- and heteroatom-centred radicals, each with the reason, and 12 polarity-matching questions (which of two partners a radical reacts with faster)
- Regioselectivity: 9 questions on radical chains (HBr with peroxides, bromination with Br₂ and light, NBS) and on Minisci and Giese additions and hydrogen-atom transfer
- A 2D structure for each radical, with the radical centre highlighted
- A Theory page on radical philicity: what raises or lowers the SOMO, ambiphilic radicals, polarity in hydrogen-atom transfer and in additions, and why there is no Mayr scale for radicals, with references
- Easy and Hard levels: Easy leaves out the harder questions

## Sources

The philicity and polarity-matching questions follow F. Parsaee, M. C. Senarathna, P. B. Kannangara, S. N. Alexander, P. D. E. Arche, E. R. Welin, *Nat. Rev. Chem.* **2021**, 5, 486 ([doi:10.1038/s41570-021-00284-3](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41570-021-00284-3)); each answer names the paper it follows. The regioselectivity questions and their explanations were written for this app. The Theory page lists its references. Structures are drawn with [RDKit](https://www.rdkit.org).

## How to cite

If you use Radical Learn in a course, a worksheet or a paper, please cite it:

> Bindschaedler, Q. *Radical Learn* (2026). ChemTrain. https://github.com/ChemTrain/radical-learn

GitHub's **Cite this repository** button (from `CITATION.cff`) gives the same reference in APA and BibTeX.
